---
title: "Resources"
order: 118
---

This module introduces no new regulation, standard, or framework, and no new source was fetched
for it. It crosswalks ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library) vocabulary — the
learner's own professional background, never itself cited to a specific AXELOS/PeopleCert
publication anywhere in this curriculum — onto AABB's (Association for the Advancement of Blood
& Biotherapies) own QSE (Quality System Essential) taxonomy and onto the eQMS's (electronic
quality-management system's) own already-built record from `grc-frameworks-and-risk-management`.
The links below are the direct inputs this module maps against, plus the already-verified AABB
page this course's own prior module relied on.

- **[AABB: Updated Quality Systems
  Essentials](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/about-aabb-standards/updated-quality-systems-essentials)**
  — AABB's own current page on the QSE framework, including QSE 3 (Equipment) and QSE 9 (Process
  Improvement), the two QSE themes this module names and maps against without quoting any
  Standards text. The same link `aabb-qse-framework`'s own resources page and
  `the-aabb-assessment-process`'s resources page already verified and used — reused here rather
  than re-checked from scratch. Use it to confirm each QSE's theme and scope in AABB's own words;
  don't cite a standard number from it.

- **[The AABB quality system at a
  glance](../../quality-system-essentials/aabb-qse-framework/index.qmd)** — the
  `quality-system-essentials` module that first named and listed all ten QSEs, including QSE 3 and
  QSE 9, the two this module's crosswalks map onto. Read it for the full taxonomy and the
  discipline of naming a QSE by theme without quoting AABB's own Standards text — the exact
  pattern this module follows.

- **[Risk Management Frameworks Side by
  Side](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/risk-frameworks-side-by-side/index.qmd)** and
  **[Categorize and Select
  Controls](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/categorize-and-select-controls/index.qmd)**
  — the two `grc-frameworks-and-risk-management` modules this module's running artifact draws its
  eQMS facts from: that it holds CAPA records, document control, and internal-audit logs across
  all three sites, replacing an older BECS (Blood Establishment Computer Software)-adjacent
  tracking tool and, at Fairview specifically, a paper-based process. Read either one for the
  eQMS's full categorization reasoning and control-family selection, which this module references
  by name but doesn't redevelop.

- **[Staying Validated: Changes, Patches, and Periodic
  Review](../../csv-and-becs/validated-state-lifecycle-and-patching/index.qmd)** — the
  `csv-and-becs` module this module's CMDB crosswalk names, reference only, for BECS's own
  validation lifecycle (a validated state, periodic review, and revalidation triggered by change)
  — the fuller version of the qualification concept a plain CMDB entry doesn't carry by default.

- **[ITIL-to-QSE Crosswalk: Change and
  Problem](../itil-to-qse-crosswalk-change-and-problem/index.qmd)** — this course's own module 1,
  for the same honest-mapping method this module continues (same discipline, narrower or stricter
  gate — never "basically identical") and for the `change-control-for-regulated-systems` and
  `capa-root-cause-to-effectiveness` references this module's QSE 9 crosswalk builds on without
  re-quoting.

- **[Key Concepts | Service Configuration Management | PeopleCert | Axelos | 1WorldTraining.com
  |](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sAdlGl7dM38)** (1 World Training Official Channel, from
  oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A training provider's walkthrough of
  ITIL 4 service configuration management's key concepts (CIs, the CMDB). Generic ITSM training,
  not blood- or validation-specific, and not published by PeopleCert/Axelos themselves — treat it
  as a refresher on the vocabulary, not as an authority. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: What is a CMDB?](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/it-asset-management/cmdb)** — a
  vendor-published but tool-neutral explainer of configuration items, relationships, and why
  change and incident work lean on the CMDB. Read it to see the ITSM side of Crosswalk 1 in
  plain language before you map it onto an equipment inventory. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cloudaware: ITIL CMDB, a practical guide to ITIL 4 service configuration
  management](https://cloudaware.com/blog/itil-cmdb/)** — an industry explainer on how ITIL 4
  frames the CMDB inside the service configuration management practice. Useful for the
  vocabulary the Director's own team uses. It is a vendor blog, so read it as practitioner
  commentary, not as ITIL's own text. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[PeopleCert: ITIL 4
  Foundation](https://www.peoplecert.org/browse-certifications/it-governance-and-service-management/ITIL-1/itil-4-foundation-2565)**
  — the ITIL 4 certification body's own page for the Foundation level, where the practices this
  module borrows vocabulary from (service configuration management, continual improvement) are
  taught. Use it to see how the framework's owner describes it. This curriculum never cites ITIL
  to a specific publication or page. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: General Principles of Software
  Validation](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/general-principles-software-validation)**
  — FDA's own guidance page on software validation, the regulator-side counterpart to the
  "qualification/validation status" field a plain CMDB entry lacks. Read it for why a system
  inventory is expected to say whether software is validated for its intended use. Guidance, not
  binding regulation. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 606.60, Equipment](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.60)** —
  Cornell's mirror of the FDA regulation on equipment used in blood establishments, the
  federal-regulation neighbor of AABB's QSE 3 (Equipment) theme. This lesson does not quote it;
  read it to see the regulator's own wording on equipment before comparing it with a CMDB entry.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ISPE: GAMP 5 Guide, 2nd
  Edition](https://www.ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-5-guide-2nd-edition)** —
  the pharmaceutical-industry professional body's catalogue page for its widely used guide to
  validating computerized systems. Useful background for how regulated industries keep a
  validated-system inventory. The guide itself is a paid publication, and this page is only its
  description. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-128: Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management of Information
  Systems](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/128/upd1/final)** — NIST's public guide to
  configuration management as a security discipline: baselines, change control, and monitoring
  of system configuration. It bridges this module's CMDB crosswalk toward module 3's RMF
  material. Read it for the government's version of "know exactly what you have and how it is
  configured." Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
